clue.text: King has novel bound in gold — it's the real McCoy!

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the novel's title is enclosed, as if tied up, within the word for gold

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
She is the adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a gold-bound royal novel is the genuine article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective but names a book: She, by H. Rider Haggard. OR is gold in heraldry, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher, literally fit by Jewish dietary law, is slang for genuine or legitimate, as is the idiom about the real McCoy.

clue.text: Description of The Ring, seen by means of a link-up

parts.note: a chain link is a ring-shaped O, and 'up' places it at the top of this down entry
PER means by means of, followed by A as written

explanation.surface: Someone says a ring was spotted thanks to some connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like jewellery, but it is Wagner's cycle of music dramas. The O comes from 'link', a round chain link, set 'up' above PER A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle is a set of four sung stage works, the musical genre named here.

clue.text: Rather unusual, during squeeze, to obtain floor covering

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come in the middle of the squeeze, inside it in time and in space

parts.note: a hug is a squeeze

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of Rather appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd instruction: squeeze something to get a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeeze' reads as a verb in the surface but supplies the outer letters; 'unusual' marks the anagram and 'during' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is a small mat laid before a fireplace, covering part of the floor.

clue.text: Point raised by everybody in trains? Indeed

indicators.note: the point and everybody sit inside the abbreviation for trains

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation of railway, a system of trains

indicators.note: in a down entry, the point is held up above the word for everybody, so it comes first

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A question about a remark raised by all the passengers, then a confirming 'Indeed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised by' sets E above ALL in this down light; 'in' puts the pair inside RY, the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Really and indeed are both interjections expressing emphasis or mild surprise.

clue.text: Stockbreeder's little' girl and boy featured in Melville?

indicators.note: the two small letters appear inside the novelist's first name, like actors in a film

parts.note: Herman Melville wrote Moby-Dick
D is the abbreviation for daughter, a little version of girl
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Asks whether a breeder's daughter and son appeared in a Melville novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' puts D and S, the genealogical abbreviations for daughter and son, inside HERMAN, Melville's first name. The stray apostrophe after 'little' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman tends or raises cattle, the work of someone who keeps livestock.

clue.text: Moving a rich chap to op, it was taken by doctors once

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges a rich chap to op, it into a new order

parts.words: a rich chap to op, it

explanation.surface: A wealthy man being wheeled to his operation, with a note about doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' is the anagram signal; the surface sends a rich patient to theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hippocratic oath was the pledge of medical ethics that physicians traditionally swore on qualifying.

clue.text: Investigative study concerning south-eastern chief

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
arch as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A study looking into a chief from the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic investigation to establish facts.

clue.text: Put to sea about noon, being a slow mover

indicators.note: the sailing word goes round the noon letter

parts.note: to sail is to put to sea

explanation.surface: Setting sail around midday, in a sluggish vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are proverbially sluggish creatures, the classic example of slow movement.

clue.text: A complex, network designed, it's said, to cause bewilderment

parts.note: a maze is a complex network of paths

parts.note: meant means designed or intended

explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' means MEANT (designed) is spelt as it sounds, MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is astonishment or stunned wonder.

clue.text: In the wild, trace pumas' bones

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of trace pumas' run free into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tracking pumas in nature by their skeletons.
explanation.definitionFit: The metacarpus is the group of five bones in the hand between wrist and fingers.

clue.text: A ludicrous set-back for a furniture designer

indicators.note: set back means the word for ludicrous is turned to read backwards

parts.note: mad means absurd or ludicrous

explanation.surface: A designer suffers an absurd reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' reverses the word for ludicrous. Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect and furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam, the Georgian architect, also designed furniture in his neoclassical style.

clue.text: Royal archer imprisoned by Chinese leader in tower

indicators.note: the royal archer is held inside the Chinese leader's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong led communist China
William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A royal bowman is locked in a tower by Mao.
explanation.walkthrough: The archer is William Tell, not a royal one. Martello towers are small round forts built along the British coast against Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello is a small circular coastal fort of the Napoleonic era.

clue.text: It's related to a student song

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
a Lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A claim about something linked to a student's song.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a student driver's car; LIED is a German art song.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means connected or akin, as in allied subjects.

clue.text: Incentive to shoot?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a reward will encourage someone to fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a goad or stimulus; it is also a short side branch that sprouts on a fruit tree.

clue.text: Play not finished at Sunningdale's last hole

indicators.note: the word for play stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to perform is to play, as music or a part

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of Sunningdale's

explanation.surface: A golfer leaves a round unfinished at the final hole at Sunningdale.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunningdale is an English golf club, so 'hole' looks like golf; it is the verb. 'not finished' cuts PERFORM to PERFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce, making holes through something; hole is the verb here.

clue.text: Skip the outing of the choir, etc

indicators.note: an outing takes the letters of choir and etc out for a jaunt, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' is not missing the outing but the definition; 'outing of' rearranges CHOIR and ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ricochet is to rebound off a surface, as a stone skips across water.

clue.text: Type of gemstone the Bruce clan distributed

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of Bruce and clan are spread out and dealt again

explanation.surface: Robert the Bruce's Scottish clan handed out a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red garnet cut with a rounded top.

clue.text: Game presumably played according to this code

definitions.text: Game presumably played according to this code

parts.words: Game presumably played according to this code
parts.note: a card game whose name is shared with a French emperor, whose legal code would presumably govern how it is played

explanation.surface: Musing on which rulebook governs a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Code Napoleon is the French civil code, so the card game's rules are said, as a pun, to follow it. Nap is a British trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, or nap, is a card game, and the emperor of that name gave France its civil code.

clue.text: Priest has an allowance for delivering a bouquet

A stands for an
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant means sweet-smelling, giving off the aroma a wine-taster calls its nose.

clue.text: Some soldiers embrace it as a religious act

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

clue.text: Draughts encountered in a prime minister's residence

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British game of checkers, also called chequers. Chequers is the British prime minister's country house in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Part of tree topped at the farm

parts.note: a branch is part of a tree

clue.text: Welshman seizes English money, disappearing quickly
